Secondly, As there ſhouldshould not be a neglect of this Duty, ſoso there ſhouldshould be great care taken that we anſweranswer the Will of God herein, wherein His Name and Honour is ſoso much concerned, in ReſpectRespect of his Love to, and Care of his Church; therefore the greaeſtgreaest diligence ſhouldshould be taken that the Rules He has given be duly obſervedobserved, and Applications made of the Qualifications laid down, in reſpectrespect of all ſuchsuch that are called unto Office: The outward Call is an Act of the Church, the

div.head: The GoſpelGospel Miniſter'sMinister's Maintenance Vindicated.
div.p:
ANDAnd indeed, it ſeemsseems to us a thing Grievous as well as Strange, that any People ſhouldshould be ſoso be clouded in their UnderſtandingsUnderstandings, as in the leaſtleast

Our main BuſineſsBusiness at this time, is not only to AſſertAssert the Miniſter'sMinister's Maintenance to be an InſtitutionInstitution of ChriſtChrist; but alſoalso, to prove it ſoso to be, and that to with-hold it from them by a Church, who is able comfortably to provide for them, is a great and crying Sin, and will be attended (we fear unleſsunless prevented by an unfeigned Repentance and Reformation) with ſeveresevere Judgment from the Holy God, who will not always bear with the Ignorant, much leſsless, the willful neglect of his own Holy Law, contained ſoso expreſlyexpressly in his ſacredsacred Word, and that we may do this the more effectually, we ſhallshall in the firſtfirst place cite thoſethose Scriptures, upon which we ground the Truth of what we AſſertAssert and Plead f • or.

This alſoalso agrees with what the ſamesame great ApoſtleApostle ſaithsaith, Gal. 6.6. Let him that is taught in the Word, Communicate to him that Teacheth in all good Things: Is not this think ye a Precept? Is not this directly

Thou haſthast not ſhewedshowed that Zeal for the True God, which ſomesome have ſhewedshowed for a FalſeFalse One: Nor that Care of, and Love to the True WorſhipWorship of God, which others have ſhewedshowed for Idolatry: May not theſethese Carnal and AntichriſtianAntichristian Heathens one Day riſerise up in Judgment againſtagainst you?

ObjObi. But may be you will Object and ſaysay, 'tis no marvel the PapiſtsPapists give ſoso
plentifully becauſebecause they think to merit Heaven thereby.

AnſwAnsw. What then? Will not you do as much for the Honour of God, and to promote his IntereſtInterest in the VVorldWorld, as thou wilt do for the Salvation of thine own Soul? If thou haſthast Eternal Life meerly of Grace, or through the Favour and Mercy of God, and Merits of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist? How much the more ſhouldshould this lay thee under an Obligation to be Bountiful and Liberal, to further and carry on, and promote the GoſpelGospel, and the Glory of God in the VVorldWorld? orOr have you a mind to betray your own Sincerity? Doth not Grace teach you better Doctrine, even to prefer the Honour of God, above whatſoeverwhatsoever is dear to you on Earth.

Thirteenthly, This will render your MiniſtersMinisters inexcuſableinexcusable, if they do not faithfully diſchargedischarge their Duties in every ReſpectRespect, to God and his People; we mean, when you diſchargedischarge your Duties to them, according to the Law
of ChriſtChrist, and Rule of JuſticeJustice and RighteouſneſsRighteousness: What will they have to ſaysay, to excuſeexcuse their RemiſsneſsRemissness and OmiſſionsOmissions in a painful ſtudyingstudying Mediation, and preaching the VVordWord, and in viſitingvisiting the Flock, when you have freed them from all manner of worldly Snares and Incumbrances, and comfortably provided for them all good Things? But on the contrary, if they come forth unprepared, and feed you with Food that hath little Soul NouriſhmentNourishment in it: How can you blame them? orOr if they never go about all the Year to know the State of the Flock as their Duty is, have they not a ready AnſwerAnswer and ExcuſeExcuse? i. eE. VVhatWhat ſhallshall become of our poor Families? VVhatWhat can you ſaysay to them? Can you excuſeexcuse them from indiſpenſibleindispensible Duties? And ſaysay we will be contented with what Service you are able to do, and all to ſavesave your PurſesPurses: the Lord open your UnderſtandingsUnderstandings, and ſhewshow you the great Evil there is in this neglect, in not complying with the VVillWill of God,
in communicating all good Things to them, who Preach the GoſpelGospel to you. And is it not from hence there is ſuchsuch a complaint in ſomesome parts of the Country, for want of the ſavingsaving Food of God's Word? We hear daily what a vaſtvast bleſſingblessing thoſethose Elders and MiniſtersMinisters are of to the People whereabouts they live, who are provided for by the Churches, over what others be who are not taken off of their ſecularsecular Affairs, being not maintained by the People; one MiniſterMinister may do more than ſeveralseveral ſuchsuch do or can do. BeſidesBesides, when once you come to acquit your ſelvesselves, as good ChriſtiansChristians ought in this CaſeCase; with what Comfort may you be able to give up your Account to ChriſtChrist? And with Joy and much Soul Peace lye down, not only in your Beds; but alſoalso in your Graves, when you come to Dye.

div.head: Motives to preſspress the Duty of the MiniſtersMinisters Maintenance, with an AnſwerAnswer to other Objections.
div.p:
1. COnſiderConsider well, and remember that your PaſtorsPastors are the MiniſtersMinisters; nay, the AmbaſſadoursAmbassadours of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist; ſuchsuch who repreſentrepresent his Sacred MajeſtyMajesty, and have his CommiſſionCommission, for what they act and do in his Name, and diſpeneedispenee the MyſteriesMysteries of God to you, according to their Duty; therefore the Lord JeſusJesus will account that done to HimſelfHimself, which is done to his MiniſtersMinisters: He that receiveth you (ſaithsaith he) receiveth me, and he that deſpiſethdespiseth you, deſpiſethdespiseth me, Mat. 10.40. Luke 10.16. If the Name and Authority of ChriſtChrist will beget an aw in you,
or his MatchleſsMatchless and UnſpeakableUnspeakable Love Influence your Souls; there is no doubt but his word will abide upon you, and cauſecause you to diſchargedischarge the Duty we have preſſedpressed upon your Spirits. If you acknowledge a Religious ReſpectRespect and Reverence due to the Son of God, exerciſeexercise it in a humble Obedience to his word; and if you Love him and value his GoſpelGospel, treat not his MiniſtersMinisters in an unworthy manner: Have you not called them off from other BuſineſsBusiness? And are they not your Servants? And is not from thence a GoſpelGospel Maintenance due to them from you, as is the wages of your other Servants? Tho we fear ſomesome give more to the meaneſtmeanest Servants in their HouſeHouse, than they to give to the MiniſtersMinisters of ChriſtChrist.

2. 'Tis'tis evident, they have a great Charge committed to their TruſtTrust, they watch for your Souls, as they who muſtmust give an account, Heb. 13.17. And therefore you ought to conſiderconsider them, and pity them, and endeavour to aſſiſtassist them, and put them into the beſtbest Capacity
you are able to do, that they may make full proof of their MiniſtryMinistry, and be free from the Blood of all Men; 'tis the BuſineſsBusiness of your own Salvation, and concern of your precious and immortal Souls, that your MiniſtersMinisters are imployedemployed in; and therefore 'tis much more your own IntereſtInterest than his, and from hence ought to make ConſcienceConscience of your Duty; for if they can't give their account with Joy, that will not be profitable for you: And how can they give an acccount of Joy concerning you, when you have neglected one great and indiſpenſibleindispensible Duty, by which means they were rendredrendered unable to perform their VVorkWork, as became them? Nor can indeed the MiniſtryMinistry ever be effectual to your Souls, if you be not ſinceresincere in Obedience under it: BeſidesBesides, as one obſervesobserves, will you be leſsless Careful for your Souls, and their Eternal wellfare, than for your Bodies, and the Comforts of a Temporal Life? Can you be content to lay out your Strength and SubſtanceSubstance
to provide for theſethese, and neglect the other? Is it not ſadsad, ſaithsaith one to conſiderconsider, How many there are among ProfeſſorsProfessors, that live in this World, as if there were no Truth in the report of that which is to come, and have the meaneſtmeanest eſteemesteem of the moſtmost neceſſarynecessary means of Salvation? viz. The Word and Ordinances of ChriſtChrist, and a GoſpelGospel MiniſtryMinistry; ſomesome can expend perhaps an hundred Pounds per Annum, more or leſsless, for Ornaments or Delights to Adorn a frail CarcaſeCarcase, but will grudg half ſoso much for the poor Saints, or to the ſupportsupport of the WorſhipWorship of the GoſpelGospel, and his ſinkingsinking IntereſtInterest.

3. ConſiderConsider how many Temptations and Soul diſcouragingdiscouraging VVeakneſſesWeaknesses your MiniſtersMinisters lye under continually, both from within and without, if ſenſiblesensible of the greatneſsgreatness of their VVorkWork; and of their own inſufficiencyinsufficiency: You know not their Fears, their Cares, their Tears, and how hard they are put to it to keep up in their VVorkWork, finding ſuchsuch ſtrongstrong OppoſitionsOppositions made againſtagainst them by the Enemy, continually, ſoso
that you had need to Strengthen, Comfort, and IncourageEncourage them, as much as you can; and not to add to their Sorrow, and make them ſerveserve you in wants and neceſſitiesnecessities.

4. We might tell you alſoalso what the ApoſtleApostle ſayssays in reſpectrespect of his Liberty as a MiniſterMinister, in forbearing to Work at all: Will any of you ſaysay your MiniſtersMinisters muſtmust labour and provide for themſelvesthemselves, when God hath Ordained the contrary; and alſoalso when the ApoſtleApostle ſaithsaith, he had power to forbear Working? See 1 Cor. 9.6. Or I only and Barnabas, Have we not power to forbear Working? We certainly (as well as the reſtrest of Chriſt'sChrist's MiniſtersMinisters) if we will run out to the utmoſtutmost end of the Line of our Liberty in things, without having regard to your CircumſtancesCircumstances, might forbear Working with our Hands, and expect that thoſethose among whom we Labour ſhouldshould maintain it. So the Annotators render it. Now, you would think this a hard thing, ſhouldshould any of your PaſtorsPastors make uſeuse
of their Liberty; yet if they ſhouldshould do it, provided they were Faithful in their Work and Office, knowing alſoalso your Ability, we would know whether any of you could charge them with Sin, as we know you may and ought other PerſonsPersons, who work not and though the ApoſtleApostle did ſometimessometimes Work, it was of choice, and to prevent the glorying of thoſethose falſefalse ApoſtlesApostles, and for ſomesome other ReaſonsReasons, which upon ſpecialspecial CircumſtancesCircumstances for that time he mentioneth, and yet he accounts it amongſtamongst his Afflictions.
QueſtQuest. Ought a PaſtorPastor or MiniſterMinister to make Terms with the Church about his Maintenance, before he take the Charge of them?

AnſwAnsw. We aſſertassert for no ſuchsuch thing, he is to take the Charge freely, and of a ready Mind: But we ſaysay there is as indiſpenſableindispensable a Duty lies upon the People to provide Carnal or Temporal good Things for him, as there lies upon him to provide Spiritual good
Things for them, and to give him Grounds to Believe they will be Faithful to ChriſtChrist and to him, in their duty upon that account.
QueſtQuest. But what ſhallshall that Church do, who are not able to allow a ſufficientsufficient Maintenance to their PaſtorPastor?
AnſwAnsw. We have a Three-fold AnſwerAnswer to this QueſtionQuestion.

FirſtFirst, If through the Poverty of the Church they cannot provide for their MiniſterMinister, they may make their CaſeCase and CircumſtanceCircumstance known to other SiſterSister Churches, and deſiredesire their Aid and AſſiſtanceAssistance herein; but if they can have none, and the Church do their Duty to the utmoſtutmost themſelvesthemselves, and yet they are not able to ſupplysupply his NeceſſitiesNecessities, then he muſtmust be contented to ſuffersuffer with the Church. But

2. If God BleſsBless a Congregation with a plentiful Portion of this Worlds Good, it is their Duty to make their MiniſtersMinisters a Party with them in their
FlouriſhingFlourishing Condition (and as a late Author ſaithsaith) ConſideringConsidering the Place and ImploymentEmployment he is in, and the Service he attends, it would be extreamly unworthy to think they have done enough, if his preſſingpressing NeceſſitiesNecessities be anſweredanswered; whilſtwhilst they themſelvesthemselves abound in Superfluities. But if the Congregation be poor, and there is no helps to he had, then their MiniſterMinister muſtmust and ought to be content to be poor with them; yea, rejoyce to approve himſelfhimself a MiniſterMinister of ChriſtChrist, (as Paul did) by Hunger and NakedneſsNakedness, if the Providence of God call him thereto; but whilſtwhilst it is in the power of their Hands to provide better for him, God expects it from them; and let none deceive themſelvesthemselves, GOD is not mocked, nor will he ſuffersuffer his Commands to be ſlightedslighted and evaded, without rendringrendering a juſtjust rebuke to the Offender, For whatſoeverwhatsoever a Man Soweth that ſhallshall he Reap. Yet neceſſitynecessity is laid upon Chriſt'sChrist's MiniſtersMinisters, and woe be to them if they Preach not the GoſpelGospel.

3. It may deſervedeserve our moſtmost mature ConſiderationConsideration, whether a People may ſafelysafely conſtituteconstitute themſelvesthemselves into a Church State, when not able to provide for a MiniſtryMinistry, eſpeciallyespecially as the CaſeCase may be circumſtancedcircumstanced; for poſſiblypossibly they might very well joyn themſelvesthemselves to another Congregation near unto them, and be a great help to ſuchsuch a Church, being Imbodied with them. And this we do ſaysay, For a People to put themſelvesthemselves into a Church State, is one of the moſtmost weightieſtweightiest Things in the World, and ought with as great Care and ConſiderationConsideration to be done; we concluding in ſomesome places where there are many Churches near to each other, it would be far better for ſomesome of thoſethose ſmallsmall and inſufficientinsufficient Societies to unite themſelvesthemselves to ſomesome other Congregation; and by that means the weight of thoſethose IndiſpencibleIndispencible Duties and Obligations that are incumbent on them, would with much more eaſeease be borne and anſweredanswered, to the Honour of ChriſtChrist, Reputation of the GoſpelGospel,
and their own Edification: Moreover, if all ChriſtiansChristians ought to conſiderconsider whether they may or ought to put themſelvesthemselves into a Church State, except they have PerſonsPersons fitly qualified and furniſhedfurnished with Gifts and Graces for the MiniſtryMinistry; which if they may not ſafelysafely do, then by the ſamesame parity of reaſonreason ought they to conſiderconsider whether they may proceed therein, if they know their own InſufficiencyInsufficiency in reſpectrespect of their making a GoſpelGospel ProviſionProvision for their Maintenance, unleſsunless they live remote from any other Church, and ſoso neceſſitynecessity put them upon their ſoso doing.
ObjObi. But is not this to build, that which you your ſelvesselves have deſtroyeddestroyed, viz. Have you not diſclaimeddisclaimed against ſuchsuch who Preach for Hire?

AnſwAnsw. We never went about we hope to deſtroydestroy any InſtitutionInstitution or Ordinance of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist, as the MiniſtersMinisters Maintenance is, as has ſufficientlysufficiently
been proved. But for Men to Preach for Hire, to make that their End, we mean in Preaching the GoſpelGospel, we ſtillstill utterly diſclaimdisclaim any ſuchsuch Practice, and ſaysay 'tis a low, carnal, and haſehas End and DeſignDesign, and unworthy of any ChriſtianChristian Man.

2. We have always diſowneddisowned, or do diſclaimdisclaim againſtagainst Tythes or the Tenths of Mens IncreaſeIncrease, declaring that they are not the right of any GoſpelGospel MiniſtersMinisters by the Law of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist, or the due of the MiniſtersMinisters of the New TeſtamentTestament, by the appointment of the Lord JeſusJesus; being only a MoſaicalMosaical Rite, and that Law to be Abrogated, as Aarons PrieſthoodPriesthood is.

3. We have always diſowneddisowned and declared againſtagainst ſuchsuch MiniſtersMinisters, who uſeuse to ſtrivestrive to compellcompel Men by outward force to Pay them what they call their dues, it looking ſoso much like an AntichriſtianAntichristian Spirit and Practice, and not agreeable to the GoſpelGospel of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist; were Love to ChriſtChrist, and the ſencesence of Duty, we find ought to be
the only prevailing Argument to excite and provoke every Man to his Duty in this great CaſeCase. Moreover you muſtmust take heed you are not prejudiced againſtagainst your Dutys from miſtakenmistaken and falſefalse ConcluſionsConclusions; becauſebecause ſomesome will not Preach unleſsunless you put into their Mouths, and ſoso make a meer Trade of Preaching. VVillWill you not anſweranswer the requirement of God to thoſethose who are the Faithful MiniſtersMinisters of his Word? BecauſeBecause ſomesome will not relieve their Poor, unleſsunless they are forced to do it, Will you diſowndisown your Duty to the poor Saints, and not relieve them, but Object and ſaysay, 'tis too much like the National practice? Or, do you not like Preaching after that manner, i. eE. with a Text, Doctrine, ReaſonsReasons, and Application; becauſebecause ſuchsuch, and ſuchsuch do ſoso, whom you diſowndisown, and cannot have Communion with. Let all ſuchsuch weak Objections be avoided, and mentioned no more for ever.

Object. You have we fear ever done it; for though we do belive 'tis the duty of the Churches to allow to their PaſtorsPastors a comfortable Maintenance, who are low in the World, and ſoso expoſedexposed to the diſtractingdistracting Cares of this Life, and thereby hindredhindered in the diſchargedischarge of their Duty in the MiniſtryMinistry. Yet for rich Men who need it not, to have an allowance, we ſeesee no reaſonreason for that.

AnſwAnsw. We AnſwerAnswer, It is not an act of Charity (to MiniſtersMinisters that are poor) we plead for, But we have proved it is an Ordinance of God, he hath been pleaſedpleased to Ordain, that thoſethose who Preach the GoſpelGospel ſhouldshould live of the GoſpelGospel: 'Tis'tis their due as they are ChriſtsChrists MiniſtersMinisters; He is their Portion now, as well as formerly under the Law, and have therefore as much right to it, as you have to your Inheritance; and from hence he willed them when he firſtfirst ſentsent them out, to take no Money in their PurſesPurses, &c. And therefore the
State of ſuchsuch you ſpeakspeak of, can't exempt you from that Ordinance, nor your duty to them; beſidesbesides, is it fitting (think you) that ſuchsuch MiniſterMinister who have EſtatesEstates ſhouldshould waſtewaste their SubſtanceSubstance, and injure their Children in their FaithfulneſsFaithfulness to ChriſtChrist in Preaching the GoſpelGospel, and in the ſervicesservices of your Souls: For their Work is ſuchsuch, that it calls for all their time and uttermoſtuttermost dilligence (in a right diſchargedischarge of their Duty therein) and therefore thereby they are prevented of Improving what they have, for the future comfort and advantage of their Families: Nay, and we have heard to our great trouble, how ſomesome worthy Men, who have Laboured fully to improve their MiniſtryMinistry (through the Peoples neglect of their duty to them) have in proceſsprocess of time ſunksunk in their EſtatesEstates, and in Truth have been brought to a low Condition; for 'tis rare to ſeesee a PaſtorPastor of our Churches to abound in Riches: Tho ſomesome (BleſſedBlessed be God) may be indifferent well to
paſspass in the World: now to expoſeexpose a rich man to Poverty, or to let a poor man ſhiftshift for himſelfhimself under wants and neceſſitiesnecessities, are Evils much of the like nature: and for a prevention of both, God hath ordered it ſoso, that neither of theſethese things ſhouldshould, or ought to be. Therefore this neglect (in ſhortshort) expoſethexposeth MiniſtersMinisters to Temptations (conſideringconsidering the moral Duty that lies upon them, in common with other men to provide for their Families) namely, to content themſelvesthemselves in doing but one part of their Work, viz. to Preach a Sermon or two in the Week, &c. Now our deſiresdesires are that they may all be wholly ſequeſtredsequestred to the Lord's Work and Service; and not be other ways imploying themſelvesthemselves, when they ſhouldshould be Preaching the Kingdom of God, but to Labour to fulfill their MiniſtryMinistry they have received of the Lord, ſoso that they may have their Accounts to give up with Joy in the Day of ChriſtChrist.
Object. But our Church is ſmallsmall, and our PaſtorPastor can't take up all his time in the Lord's Work.

AnſwerAnswer. We AnſwerAnswer, If he wants work, who will hinder him from following of his ſecularsecular BuſineſsBusiness, provided he doth faithfully and fully diſchargedischarge every part of the duty of his Place and Function? But do not the Neighbouring Villages, and places adjacent want the GoſpelGospel, having no Bread for their Souls, and this too by reaſonreason ſuchsuch PaſtorsPastors are unconcerned in this matter? andAnd by which means 'tis doubtleſsdoubtless that the Glorious GoſpelGospel is no more promulgated up and down in dark and blind corners of this Nation, nor the Church increaſesincreases no more; BeſidesBesides do not many poor Sinners daily periſhperish hereby for want of Knowledg? Brethren, 'tis not for our ſelvesselves, but for the Lord, and his ſinkingsinking IntereſtInterest that we plead for; it grieves our Souls to hear what cries there are in many parts
of this Kindom for want of Bread, ſomesome being forc'd, we hear, to go twelve or ſixteensixteen Miles to hear a Sermon; now if MiniſtersMinisters of Churches made it their whole BuſineſsBusiness to Preach the Word, and concern themſelvesthemselves for the promoting of the Truth, it would not be as it is at this very time; nor can we think it ſhouldshould be otherwiſeotherwise, unleſsunless we had a travelling MiniſtryMinistry (which we fear we ſhallshall hardly find) unleſsunless PaſtorsPastors and Teachers in the reſpectiverespective Churches were taken off of all Incumbrances, and ſoso give themſelvesthemselves up to the MiniſtryMinistry of the VVordWord.

God has done great things for us, and hath opened a mighty door, and ſhallshall not we do ſomesome great thing for Him? The CaſeCase, BleſſedBlessed be the Lord, is much altered: You may come now into any Town and none dare forbid you, (if any one will but entertain you) and Preach the GoſpelGospel; And ſhallshall we not take care to anſweranswer this Mercy; and do what we can that the poor Blind
VVorldWorld may be Inlightened, and brought to the ſavingsaving Knowledge of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist? If the preſentpresent Providence of God be not anſweredanswered by a due Improvement to his Glory, and the furtherance of the GoſpelGospel: VVeWe may ſaysay with Solomon, Why is there a price in the Hand of a Fool, ſeeingseeing he hath no Heart to it, Prov. 17.16. By this time we hope you may more clearly underſtandunderstand us, and what we drive at, and earneſtlyearnestly deſiredesire to ſeesee accompliſhedaccomplished, viz. That MiniſtersMinisters may not only bear that Name, but with all FaithfulneſsFaithfulness do the VVorkWork, they are called to; 'tis not to preſspress our People to MiniſterMinister to ſuchsuch Preachers who are Idle and Negligent in their BuſineſsBusiness, whoſewhose Hearts and Hands are in the VVorldWorld, and eagerly purſuepursue their own ſecularsecular Affairs, and matter not what becomes of the IntereſtInterest of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist.

No, 'tis to encourage the Faithful and Labourous PerſonPerson, who is willing to give himſelfhimself up to the Lord, in the DiſchargeDischarge of that great TurſtTurst
committed to him, and to Labour indeed in Chriſt'sChrist's Vineyard; it is in truth a • ſhameshame for a MiniſterMinister to receive the Lord's VVagesWages, and not do the Lord's VVorkWork; ſomesome there are in the World t • hat do not deſervedeserve the Name of Minist •… ers they doing the VVorkWork of the Lord ſoso deceitfully.

Our Churches alſoalso are 'tis like in ſomesome places in the Country but ſmallsmall, and a • re like to be ſmallersmaller, if the MiniſtryMinistry be 〈◊〉
not awakened to become more Labourous: Are there not ſuchsuch in ſomesome Towns, who are hardly known by the Inhabitants to be MiniſtersMinisters at a • ll, they are ſoso little concerned in Preaching, they are better known to be Farmers, Yeomen, and TradeſmanTradesman, then Preachers of the GoſpelGospel; they are int • angled ſoso in the Affairs of this Life, t • hat they have but little time to mind t • he great Work they are called to: We would ask ſomesome MiniſtersMinisters, whether t • hey could not do much more, Preach oftner, and in more Places, and take greater Pains, to promote the GoſpelGospel,
and gather in Souls to ChriſtChrist, than they do? Certainly they will and muſtmust ſaysay, yea, we might; VVhyWhy what is the reaſonreason of your not doing it? Ought we not with Mary to do what we can? VVeWe conclude, this OmiſſionOmission of Duty either ariſesarises from the evil of your own Hearts, or elſeelse from the RemiſneſsRemissness and Neglect of the People, in ReſpectRespect of their Duty to you. (1.) It may ariſearise from the Evil in your own Hearts, in that you have not or do not eſpouſeespouse the IntereſtInterest of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist, equal with, or above your own: Can any be contented in doing a little Service for ChriſtChrist, tho his IntereſtInterest ſinkssinks in their Hands; whilſtwhilst they thrive in their own concerns, and grow Rich in the VVorldWorld: Lord, what will become of ſuchsuch MiniſtersMinisters in the day of •
Judgment? Can they think to look •…
ChriſtChrist in the Face with Comfort, that • have been ſuchsuch ſlothfulslothful Servants; but • God forbid there ſhouldshould be any among us who mind more their • own trifling Affairs, than the great •
VVorkWork and BuſineſsBusiness of their bleſſedblessed Lord and MaſterMaster? Is this the making full Proof of your MiniſtryMinistry you have received of the Lord? Chriſt'sChrist's MiniſtersMinisters are called Labourers, but we fear ſomesome Labour but little, unleſsunless it be at their own work: ſhouldshould you be as RemiſsRemiss in your own Affairs, as poſſiblypossibly you are in the Lords, you would find quickly a decay in your EſtatesEstates, and be in a ſinkingsinking Condition in the World; which 'tis like, would ſoonsoon ſtartlestartle you, and ſtirstir you up to greater Care and InduſtryIndustry; and ought you not to be as conſiderateconsiderate in the great concernment of ChriſtChrist, his GoſpelGospel and Churches? We take it not upon us to reprehend any of you but in Love (as fellow Servants may do) to caution you; pray remember, you have the moſtmost ſacredsacred IntereſtInterest and Matters of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist committed to your TruſtTrust; 'tis the greateſtgreatest Charge in the World, and you and we muſtmust be call • ed to an Account, if Souls periſhperish in their Sins, and the Watchman gives not
ſuitablesuitable warning, the Blood of thoſethose Sinners God will require at the Watchman's Hands, Zeck. 3. MiniſtersMinisters ought to be the Light of the World, they ſhouldshould ſhineshine therefore in Life and Doctrine, to all round about where they live, that the People may know they have a Noah, a Preacher of RighteouſneſsRighteousness amongſtamongst them. But

2. This grand fault may ariſearise from the Peoples RemiſneſsRemissness of Duty to their MiniſtersMinisters; for hark, do we not hear many worthy and faithful PaſtorsPastors crying out? Alas Brethren, we are no more in the Lord's VVorkWork, no more in Preaching, in ViſitingVisiting, &c. BecauſeBecause our Families would ſuffersuffer want, and what is neceſſarynecessary for them; we ſhouldshould gladly make the GoſpelGospel our whole BuſineſsBusiness, and not only watch over, and feed our own Flocks, but Preach the GoſpelGospel up and down in Towns and Villages, lying near us, if we knew how our VVivesWives and Children might be provided for; for ſhouldshould we neglect that great Moral and indiſpenſibleindispensible
Duty, how would the Holy Name of God be reproached? Alas, our Souls are bowed down in us, we muſtmust confeſsconfess, we have daily calls to Preach, in this and that place, where to this day there has hardly been any Meeting; but we are not able to do it, and therefore, we are forc'd to ſendsend to London, that ſomesome MiniſtersMinisters might come down into our Parts, to AnſwerAnswer that great Call and Cry of Men and VVomenWomen, for want of the Bread of Life.

This is a hard CaſeCase indeed, i. eE. for the Servants of ChriſtChrist to have the due ſenſesense of the greatneſsgreatness of their work upon their Hearts, but cannot diſchargedischarge it according as they ſeesee there is a Call and OccaſionOccasion, by ReaſonReason the People neglect their Duty to them: But however, do what you can, and venture out, God will provide for you, and move upon the Hearts of ſuchsuch you Preach the GoſpelGospel to, or ſomesome other way provide for you: Improve this preſentpresent Liberty, and do not let
the Lord's HouſeHouse lie waſtewaste: Remember, NeceſſityNecessity is laid upon you, and wo be to you, if you Preach not the GoſpelGospel, be not Unbelieving, but truſttrust the Providence of God; great things he expecteth from us, who has ſoso gloriouſlygloriously and graciouſlygraciously appeared for us, and for the Land of our Nativity.

NevertheleſsNevertheless, Let none miſtakemistake us; we do not ſaysay, 'tis unlawful for Preachers to VVorkWork or follow Callings; but as Preaching doth not make VVorkingWorking unlawful, neither ſhouldshould any VVorldlyWorldly BuſineſsBusiness hinder Preaching, therefore when working with our Hands will further the GoſpelGospel, we may VVorkWork; we have a Call ſoso to do (which was once Paul's CaſeCase) but when working at Trades and Callings, does palpably tend to the hinderancehindrance of the Promulgation of the GoſpelGospel; we muſtmust give over ſuchsuch VVorkingWorking, and wholly give up our ſelvesselves to Preaching &c. 'Tis'tis but to make an Expediment, if the People ſhouldshould fail you: You know your Liberty, he that Laboured with
his Hands, hath by that Example ſetset the ConſciencesConsciences of MiniſtersMinisters at Liberty, to provide for the NeceſſitiesNecessities of this Life, by other Imployments, when they cannot Live of the GoſpelGospel; but this very thing Paul accounted amongſtamongst his Afflictions; and certainly, it muſtmust needs be a ſoresore Grief and ExerciſeExercise to any Godly Preacher in this ReſpectRespect, i. eE. when he hears People calling him, one Day to this Town to Preach, and another Day to that, and he finds he cannot AnſwerAnswer neither of their Calls, through the NeceſſitiesNecessities of his FamlyFamily; and the truth is, all do readily grant, that no poſitivepositive Duty can DiſchargeDischarge a Man from the Obligations of that pure Moral and UniverſalUniversal Duty of providing for his Families.

Brethren, you know when the HarveſtHarvest proves catching, and the Painful and Laborious HarveſtHarvest-men are taken off of their BuſineſsBusiness, then they may do a little VVorkWork for themſelvesthemselves, but when 'tis good HarveſtHarvest weather, and the HarveſtHarvest is great, and the Labourers
but few, they muſtmust ſtickstick to it and Labour hard.

Even ſoso when the late Storms of PerſecutionPersecution were upon us, many of Chriſt'sChrist's Spiritual HarveſtHarvest-men were much hindredhindered and taken off of their Work, and did may be imployemploy themſelvesthemselves otherwiſeotherwise, in their other Affairs (few being willing to open their Doors to them;) but now the Providence of God has opened a great Door for the GoſpelGospel, and ſentsent us BleſſedBlessed HarveſtHarvest Weather, and the Labourers alas! beingBeing alſoalso very few, though the HarveſtHarvest is very great: How ought we to ſtickstick to our BuſineſsBusiness?

There was never certainly ſuchsuch a Call to MiniſtersMinisters to Work for God as there is now; therefore that Servant that will not do his beſtbest at ſuchsuch an Hour, is like the Son (that Solomon ſpeaksspeaks of) that Sleeps in HarveſtHarvest and ſoso cauſethcauseth Shame. And as a wiſewise Husband-man will not neglect a fit opportunity of gathering in his Corn, upon preſumptionpresumption of
much fair Weather to come: So ought not we to loſelose the preſentpresent SeaſonSeason for gathering in Souls to ChriſtChrist, not knowing how ſoonsoon Clouds may riſerise, and another Storm overtake us, when we cannot Work for God as now we may; and if you have not ſuchsuch IncouragementEncouragement as you ought to have from the People, yet remember when Night comes, the Lord JeſusJesus will well reward you for all the pains you take in his Work; yet ſincesince our Saviour ſaithsaith the Labourer is worthy of his Hire, we can't think any (when they conſiderconsider the Matter a little better) will any way obſtructobstruct, or hinder you in your BuſineſsBusiness through their neglect of Duty to you.
Object. But doth not ChriſtChrist tell his DiſciplesDisciples? As they had freely received, ſoso they ſhouldshould freely give.

AnſwAnsw. We Believe this Text is not taken, or underſtoodunderstood according to the meaning of our Saviour; for it cannot
mean that Chriſt'sChrist's MiniſtersMinisters ſhouldshould receive neither Money, Meat, or Clothes, whilſtwhilst they are imploy'd in his Work and Service, becauſebecause in the very next VerſeVerse he bids them Provide neither Gold nor Silver, nor BraſsBrass in their PurſesPurses, nor two Coats, nor Scrip for their Journey; becauſebecause he plainly intimates all ſuchsuch things they were worthy of, and might expect them from the People to whom they Preached. Therefore 'tis an horrible abuſeabuse put upon the Text, to take the Words in that SenſeSense; as if our BleſſedBlessed MaſterMaster ſhouldshould forbid his Servants to receive a Maintenance from the People; for then indeed they might have ſaidsaid, Lord, If we muſtmust Preach ſoso freely as not to receive any thing, it behoveth us to provide well for our Journey; but ſincesince they were forbid to do ſoso, it is clear that could not be our Saviours meaning: BeſidesBesides, ſuchsuch a Sence is directly oppoſiteopposite or repugnant to thoſethose other Precepts the Lord JeſusJesus hath laid down by his ApoſtlesApostles in the EpiſtlesEpistles; wherein it is poſitivelypositively
aſſertedasserted (as you have heard) that He that is taught in the Word ought to Communicate to him that Teacheth in all good things, 1 Tim. 5.18. And that they who MiniſterMinister at the Altar ſhouldshould partake of the Altar; God having Ordained that he that Preaches the GoſpelGospel, ſhouldshould live of the GoſpelGospel, 1 Cor. 9.14. Therefore we rather are of the Opinion (in reſpectrespect to this Text) with a late worthy VVriterWriter; The Doctrine (ſayssays he) they were to Preach, they were Impowered to Confirm with Miracles; which (ſaysay they) He gives them a Charge they ſhouldshould Work freely, without receiving any Reward for them; that the Miracles might not be uſedused to their private Profit, but to the End they were appointed of God, which was the Confirmation of their Doctrine.

2. It may alſoalso teach us that MiniſtersMinisters ought not to make a Bargain with the People, or deſiredesire to know what they ſhallshall have before they enter on their Work; for he who would approve himſelfhimself a true MiniſterMinister of JeſusJesus
ChriſtChrist, ou • ght 〈◊〉 not to Preach for Hire or filthy Lu •… cres ſakesake, i. eE. that ought not to be the thing he aims at; that's a low and baſebase deſigndesign, but as you know Churches provide and ought to provide for the Poor; yet ſhouldshould any ſeekseek to come into your Communion meerly for a Maintenance, you would ſaysay he or ſheshe that did ſoso, were no better than Hypocrites, and (may ſaysay truly) yet that would not free you from communicating to poor Faithful ChriſtiansChristians. Even ſoso, if ſomesome deceitful and carnal PerſonsPersons ſhouldshould undertake the Work of the MiniſtryMinistry for filthy Lucres ſakesake, and not in Love to ChriſtChrist, and to promote his IntereſtInterest and Glory, they, doubtleſsdoubtless act contrary to this Precept of ChriſtChrist. But yet nevertheleſsnevertheless, the Church is • bound to communicate and allow a comfortable Maintenance to her Faithful MiniſtersMinisters; and as he freely, and of a ready Mind, and for Chriſt'sChrist's ſakesake, Preaches the GoſpelGospel, and is bound ſoso to do if he will approve himſelf • himself
Faithful; ſoso in like manner are the People and Churches of God bound freely and of a ready mind to MiniſterMinister to them, if they would ſhewshow to all they are Faithful ChriſtiansChristians, ſuchsuch who have an equal reſpectrespect to all ChriſtsChrists Commands and DeſireDesire, to the utmoſtutmost of their Abilities, to further and not hinder the promulgation of the GoſpelGospel in the World.

But by the way it is plain, had it not been the practice of the GoſpelGospel Churches in the ApoſtlesApostles time, to allow their PaſtorsPastors a Maintenance, what room was there for the ApoſtleApostle to caution any MiniſterMinister or Elder not to undertake the Work for filthy Lucres ſakesake, but of a ready mind. Moreover, very remarkable is it to conſiderconsider how the PrieſtsPriests of God under the Law were to receive that Portion Jehovah gave them: They were not (as Mr. AinſworthAinsworth noteth) To receive it after a baſebase or ſervileservile manner, but as Gifts due to the Lord, and to them from him: The Hebrew Canons (ſaithsaith he) ſhewshow the IſraelitesIsraelites
were to give them their Portion with Honour; and it was unlawful for the PrieſtsPriests or Levites to ſnatchsnatch away the Heave-Offering, or the Tithes; yea, ſaithsaith he, if they did but ask their Portion with their Mouth it was unlawful. Read his Annotation on Numb. 18. vV. 12. And then on Deut. 18.3. He ſaithsaith again, the PrieſtPriest might not violently take the Gifts, nor ask them with his Mouth, but he received them when they were given him with Honour.

This may teach us two things. FirſtFirst, that Chriſt'sChrist's Servants ought to take heed they ſhewshow all true and real Zeal and Love to ChriſtChrist, when they undertake his Work and Service; and not to ſhewshow ſuchsuch a ſervileservile and baſebase Spirit as to demand their Portion that God has Ordained for them, but leave it to the free will Offering of the People. Secondly, It may alſoalso teach Churches to ſeesee they do neither withhold the MiniſtersMinisters Portion from them, nor give it them grudgingly, or in an unbecoming manner, but to hand out
to them what they need with due reſpectrespect and honour, they being worthy of it, and are to receive it as their part and portion from God, and as they are His Stewards and Faithful Labourers, by Virtue of a Divine and Holy Law: Nay, and the Lord's People ought to be as careful in diſchargedischarge of this Duty to Chriſt'sChrist's MiniſtersMinisters now, as the IſraelitesIsraelites were to the Levites; tho' as we have already ſaidsaid, their Portion is not the Tithes of Mens IncreaſeIncrease, nor the FirſtFirst Fruits, which Law is Abrogated. Yet ſaithsaith Reverend AinſworthAinsworth, 'The'the Equity of that Law remaineth perpetually, as the ApoſtleApostle obſervethobserveth, Do you not know that they which MiniſterMinister about Holy things, live of the things of the Temple; and they that wait at the Altar, are partakers with the Altar: Even ſoso hath the Lord Ordained, &c. 1. Cor. 13.14. BecauſeBecause the MiniſtersMinisters of God then were injoyned to attend on His Service, he would not have them cumbred with worldly Affairs,
leaſtleast (ſaithsaith he) they ſhouldshould be hinddred from doing their Duties; as it is Written, No Man that Warreth intangleth himſelfhimself with the Affairs of this Life, that he may pleaſeplease him who hath called him to be a Soldier. 2 Tim. 3.4. From hence God hath ordered it thus for them.' Moreover, the Hebrews ſaysay from hence 'twas Levi was not counted meeet to have Inheritance in the Land of IſraelIsrael, or Spoils with his Brethren, becauſebecause he was ſeparatedseparated to Serve the Lord, and to Inherit him, and to teach his ſtraitstrait Ways, and his Just Judgments unto the People: therefore was he ſeparatedseparated from the ways of the World; they wage not War, as the reſtrest of IſraelIsrael do, neither do they Inherit nor Earn for themſelvesthemselves with the Strength of their Bodies, but they are the Lords Power (or Substance) as it is Written, Deut. 13.11. BleſsBless Lord his Power; and the BleſſedBlessed God earneth for them, as it is Written Numb. 18.20. I am thy Part and thine Inheritance. Maim. Treat. ofOf the ReleaſeRelease and Jubilee, c. 13. f. 12.

The reaſonreason of the ſamesame Law, 'tis evident of neceſſitynecessity does remain; the Work of MiniſtersMinisters is great now, and 'tis as Holy and as Honourable as ever, and the neglect of a Faithful diſchargedischarge herein, as great a Sin as it was then; and God's People have as great, nay, greater Benefit and Divine Profit by the MiniſtryMinistry of the GoſpelGospel, than thoſethose had who lived under the Law; beſidesbesides Chriſt'sChrist's Servants have the ſamesame need of it: moreover, our People are delivered from other great Burdens and vaſtvast Charges that the People of IſraelIsrael were continually at; and therefore how unjuſtunjust and unreaſonableunreasonable a thing is it to with-hold a fit and convenient Lively-hood from them. Nay, and we muſtmust ſaysay, that which any with-hold from the Servants of God, is the Lord's, and none of theirs; for he lays claim to part of their SubſtanceSubstance, as that which He has Ordained to his own ſpecialspecial ſerviceservice and uſeuse of His Faithful MiniſtersMinisters.
QueſtQuest. May every one then that Preaches expect an Allowance, though they Preach but now and then.

AnſwAnsw. That muſtmust be left to the WiſdomWisdom and ConſiderationConsideration of the Church; who ought to conſiderconsider the PerſonsPersons CircumſtancesCircumstances, with the Call he hath to Preach, &c. But principally it belongs to thoſethose who are ſetset a part to that Work, whoſewhose Strength and Time is taken up about the great Affairs of ChriſtChrist and the GoſpelGospel.

Thus we have indeavoured to diſchargedischarge our Duty as touching this great Work, and have we hope AnſweredAnswered all the material Objections any have to bring, or urge againſtagainst the MiniſtersMinisters Maintenance: But ſincesince we have a little Room we ſhallshall add ſomesome brief hints further, to ſhewshow the great charge and work of a true GoſpelGospel MiniſterMinister,
and ſoso conclude; that all may ſeesee how needful a thing it is, that every one take care to diſchargedischarge their Duty in this matter to them, whereby alſoalso the JuſtneſsJustness and RighteouſneſsRighteousness of the Law, and appointment of God herein, may yet further appear to all.

div.head: The Great and Weighty Work of a True GoſpelGospel MiniſterMinister opened.
div.p: THEThe Nature and WeightineſsWeightiness of the Work of the Faithful Servant of ChriſtChrist, together with the neceſſitynecessity and difficulty of it, we ſhallshall conſiderconsider in its parts in a brief and compendious manner.

FirſtFirst, 'Tis'tis a Holy and a ſublimesublime Office; he is placed in a very high Sphere
and Station, hence called the AmbaſſadorAmbassador of ChriſtChrist; What higher Dignity can be conferred on Man? The greatneſsgreatness of the Prince whoſewhose MeſſengersMessengers they are, ſetssets forth their Dignity; they are in Chriſt'sChrist's ſteadstead ImployedEmployed in the great Affairs of His Spiritual Kingdom; and have received Authority from Him, and are alſoalso prepared and qualified for this Sacred Work by Him, and indeed therefore ought to be blameleſsblameless, as the Stewards of God: And hence it is that thoſethose who are ſaidsaid to receive them, receive Him; and thoſethose who deſpiſedespise them, deſpiſedespise Him. O! withWith what Holy Fear, Dread, and Reverence ought they to enter upon this Work and Office, leaſtleast they ſhouldshould diſhonourdishonour their great and glorious Prince and Heavenly Soveraign, whom they repreſentrepresent! Is it not a weighty thing to be made the Mouth of ChriſtChrist?

2. Nay, and this is not all, they are intruſtedintrusted with matters of the higheſthighest moment in the World, ChriſtChrist having
committed the Management of his Glorious IntereſtsInterests, and great concerns he has on Earth into their Hands; they are ſentsent to treat with poor Sinners about Eternal Matters, even the Eternal Life, or Eternal Death and Damnation of their Precious and Immortal Souls, in and about theſethese things MiniſtersMinisters of the GoſpelGospel are Fellow Workers together with ChriſtChrist. 2. Cor. 6.1. Though but as InſtrumentsInstruments, ſervingserving him as the principal Agent, and efficient CauſeCause: He trod the Wine-PreſsPress of his Fathers Wrath alone; but in the Application of the purchaſepurchase of Man's Salvation, he admits of Fellow-workers, tho the internal Work be his, i. eE. the effects of his Spirits upon the Souls of thoſethose whoſewhose Hearts are changed; yet there is a MiniſterialMinisterial part which lyeth on the faithful DiſchargeDischarge of the Miniſter'sMinister's Duty, which conſiſtethconsisteth partly in Exhortations, Motives and Arguments, by the Ear conveyed to the Soul; and thus MiniſtersMinisters may be ſaidsaid to be Workers together with ChriſtChrist, and without him they can do
nothing, they are Workers, but they muſtmust have ChriſtChrist Work with them, or they will find that they Labour in Vain.

But is it not think you a high and moſtmost ſacredsacred Place and Office thus to be imployedemployed? May not every one of us ſaysay, who are ſufficientsufficient for theſethese things, for we are unto God (ſaithsaith the ApoſtleApostle) a ſweetsweet ſavoursavour of ChriſtChrist in them that are ſavedsaved, and in them that periſhperish, 2 Cor. 2. forFor that God whom we, ſerveserve, will not Judge of us, nor reward us according to our SucceſsSuccess (as a worthy Author obſervesobserves) but according to our FaithfulneſsFaithfulness and Diligence in his Work, we give (as if Paul ſhouldshould ſaysay) a good ſavoursavour by our Doctrine unto all, and our Labours are a ſweetsweet ſavoursavour in the NoſtrilsNostrils of God, whatever effects they have upon the Souls of Men; God accepteth of our Labours, as to good Men, to whom we are InſtrumentsInstruments of Eternal Life and Salvation; and though others deſpiſedespise the GoſpelGospel, and refuſerefuse the ſweetsweet ſoundsound thereof; yet as to them
alſoalso, we are a ſweetsweet ſavoursavour in the NoſtrilsNostrils of God, tho IſraelIsrael be not ſavedsaved, ſaithsaith the Prophet, yet I ſhallshall be glorious; it is not through any neglect in us, as to our duty if any periſhperish, but from their own WillfulneſsWillfulness and Rebellious Hearts. To the one, we are the ſavoursavour of Death unto Death, and to the other, the ſavoursavour of Life unto Life. And who is ſufficientsufficient for theſethese things. ver. 16.

As ſweetsweet ſmellssmells, which are to ſomesome pleaſantpleasant and comfortable (ſaithsaith a Worthy Author) yet are to others pernicious and deadly; ſoso it is with the ſweetsweet ſavoursavour of the GoſpelGospel; the report which we in all places make of ChriſtChrist, to ſomesome (through their unbelief, and hardneſshardness of their Heart, and fondneſsfondness of their LuſtsLusts) proveth; but the Savour of Death unto Death, hardning their Hearts to their Eternal RuineRuin and DeſtructionDestruction; but to ſuchsuch who (being ordained to Eternal Life; believe our Report, and) imbrace the GoſpelGospel, and live up to the Precepts and Rule thereof; our Preaching proves a CauſeCause of
Spiritual and Eternal Life to which that leadeth; but O how great a work is this! What Man? What Angel, is ſufficientsufficient for it? O it is a mighty VVorkWork to Preach the GoſpelGospel, as we ought to Preach it; it is that by which Faith cometh, How ſhallshall they believe on him, of whom they have not heard? And how ſhallshall they hear, without a Preacher? And how ſhallshall they Preach, except they are ſentsent? Rom. 10.14. i. eE. UnleſsUnless they have an extraordinary or ordinary MiſſionMission, i. eE. either from God more immediately (which Call is long ſincesince ceaſedceased) or elſeelse, by the Election of the Church, and Ordination of the Elders, or Presbytery; this is neceſſarynecessary in all Regular MiniſtersMinisters: How elſeelse can they duly or profitably in the Name and Authority of ChriſtChrist, preach the Word of Life? Brethren, (you who are Chriſt'sChrist's true MiniſtersMinisters being orderly called to this ſacredsacred Work,) your Preaching hath attendency, either to ſavesave, or eternally to condemn the Souls of Men; and with what trembling then,
ought this Work to be undertaken and performed; you are intruſtedintrusted with Men's Souls, and muſtmust be accountable for them; eſpeciallyespecially, ſuchsuch who are committed to your Charge; did we conſiderconsider it, and duly ponder upon it in our Minds, certainly, we ſhouldshould have little elſeelse to think upon, nor trouble our Heads and Hearts about, it would be ſuresure cauſecause us to be more Serious, and Laborious, we are perſwadedpersuaded, than we are: VVhatWhat ſhallshall we do, if through our Neglect and RemiſneſsRemissness in this great VVorkWork, any ſhouldshould die and periſhperish in their Sins? Mind what God ſaithsaith in that of Ezek. 3.18. Unto his VVatchmanWatchman, When I ſaysay unto the wicked, thou ſhaltshalt ſurelysurely dye, and thou giveſtgivest him not warning, nor ſpeakeſtspeakest to warn the wicked from his way, to ſavesave his Life, the ſamesame wicked man ſhallshall die in his Iniquity, but his Blood I will require at thine Hand; tho ſomesome do prophanely ſcoffscoff and deride, yet muſtmust we ſpeakspeak to them, and warn them, until it do appear they are ſuchsuch as will turn again
and rend us, Men muſtmust be told their Sins, and their Dangers, that ſoso we (as InſtrumentsInstruments in God's Hand) may preſervepreserve their Souls, and recal them at • once both from Sin and Death, the Man who is not warned, will certainly die in his Sins, his Ignorance will not be ſufficientsufficient to prevent his Ruin and Damnation; but if MiniſtersMinisters admoniſhadmonish him not, warn him not, that will involve them alſoalso under Guilt and Danger, God will puniſhpunish ſuchsuch MiniſtersMinisters and Watchmen, who poſſiblypossibly might have ſavedsaved thoſethose periſhingperishing Sinners, however they ought to have warned them, And

Hence how Careful was St. Paul, ſeesee Acts 20.26. thatThat ye might be pure from the Blood of all Men; he appeals to the Church of EpheſusEphesus, in that matter they knowing his great Care, FaithfulneſsFaithfulness, and unwearied InduſtryIndustry, upon every ReſpectRespect; and ſhewsshows that no Soul had been loſtlost through his default, he having ſincerelysincerely, and in all ſimplicitysimplicity declared to them the way of Life, and perſwadedpersuaded them to walk therein, and
